items.headline: September nonfarm payrolls due TONIGHT 20:30 SGT -- forecast ~89k vs August's 162k -- the binary catalyst Asia's open is waiting on
items.summary: The BLS releases the September jobs report Friday at 8:30am ET / 8:30pm SGT, with consensus around 89k versus August's 162k gain; this has not happened yet as of Friday's pre-Asia-open window. It follows two data points that already landed Thursday: ISM Manufacturing PMI cooled to 54.5% (vs 55.0% expected, and down from August's 54.6%) while its Prices Index jumped 6.8pp to 77.9% -- a soft-growth/sticky-inflation combination -- and initial jobless claims fell to 197k (vs 200k expected), still near multi-decade lows.
items.actionable: A soft payrolls print tonight would extend the rate-cut-odds relief that's been supporting silver/miners, HK tech and SGX banks via lower discount rates, while a hot print -- especially paired with Thursday's hot ISM Prices Index -- would revive the hawkish-Fed/stronger-dollar dynamic that pressures gold, silver and risk assets together; size any pre-payrolls moves at Asia's open accordingly.

items.headline: Oil jumps ~3% as US sends a third carrier strike group toward Iran and China halts October fuel exports to hoard domestic stocks
items.summary: WTI settled up roughly 2.7-3% near $92.9-93.2 and Brent briefly topped $100/bbl Thursday after reports that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group is steaming toward the Middle East (bringing the US presence there to three carrier groups, 20,000+ sailors and Marines) while President Trump weighs further strikes and denied any sanctions-relief offer to Tehran. Separately, Chinese refiners -- including PetroChina, which cancelled gasoline/jet-fuel cargoes -- suspended October product exports outside Hong Kong/Macau to preserve domestic stocks during Golden Week, tightening an already war-constrained fuel market and pushing Asian diesel swap spreads to a two-week high.
items.actionable: This is a genuine escalation (military buildup, not just rhetoric) layered on a real Chinese supply withdrawal, which argues for keeping the Houthi/Hormuz tail-risk thesis live rather than treating the earlier Gulf-export-recovery narrative as the base case -- but it also raises diesel/power input costs for the miners in the silver/gold sleeve right as bullion itself caught a safe-haven bid.

items.headline: Miners decouple from metal again: GLD +0.50%/SLV +0.94% on Iran safe-haven flow, but GDX -1.21%, SILJ -0.62%, PAAS -1.16%, Barrick -1.13% all fall
items.summary: Gold and silver ETFs caught a bid Thursday from the Iran-war escalation (safe-haven demand) even as the dollar held firm, but the mining-equity sleeve moved the other way -- a pattern market commentary attributes to miners' direct exposure to the same oil spike (higher diesel and power costs squeeze margins) plus idiosyncratic pressure on Barrick, where CEO Mark Hill said this week the North American gold-unit IPO could slip from year-end into January 2027. Newmont and other large-cap producers have shown a similar bullion-outperforms-miners pattern this week on dollar/rate-hawk jitters.
items.actionable: The bullion/miner split now has two distinct drivers -- Barrick's IPO-timeline uncertainty (company-specific) and rising energy input costs from the same Iran-driven oil rally (sector-wide) -- so a further oil spike would keep pressuring GDX/PAAS/GOLD even if gold itself extends its safe-haven bid; don't read Thursday's miner weakness as a read-through on the metal.

items.headline: Lynas to buy Meteoric Resources for A$968m all-scrip; LYC.AX sinks 8.6% to A$12.64 on dilution even as resource base grows ~79%
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths agreed to acquire ASX-listed Meteoric Resources in an all-share deal worth A$968m (0.0207 new Lynas shares per Meteoric share, a 68% premium to Meteoric's last close), giving Lynas 100% of the Caldeira rare-earth project in Brazil and lifting its measured-and-indicated REO resources by roughly 79%. The market's reaction was classic dilution-on-announcement -- Meteoric holders will own ~5.9% of the combined company, Lynas committed up to A$110m in working-capital funding for Caldeira, and the deal doesn't close until a scheme implementation expected around March 2027 -- which drove LYC.AX down 8.6% (A$13.83 to A$12.64) despite the long-term resource-expansion logic.
items.actionable: This is deal-dilution selling, not a demand or China-supply shock to the ex-China rare-earth thesis -- if anything the long-dated resource growth is bullish for Lynas's 2027+ supply story -- so the read-through to MP/UUUU (both also down Thursday, -2.54% and -2.90%, with no company-specific news found) looks more like sympathy/sector de-risking around the announcement than a fundamental reset of the watchlist.

items.headline: USA Rare Earth completes CEO transition -- Thras Moraitis replaces retiring Barbara Humpton -- as Jefferies initiates Buy with $21 target
items.summary: USA Rare Earth (USAR) announced October 1 that Thras Moraitis, previously the company's president, has formally become CEO, succeeding Barbara Humpton, who built the firm's public-private partnerships across mining, processing and magnet manufacturing. The leadership news lands alongside a fresh Jefferies initiation at Buy with a $21 price target, even though USAR shares are still down roughly 36% over the past month and 64% off their October 2025 52-week high of $43.98.
items.actionable: A clean leadership handoff plus a fresh sell-side Buy call are modest positives for the watchlist's most speculative, most-drawn-down name, but the scale of USAR's pullback versus MP's relative resilience is a reminder to size the watchlist by balance-sheet/offtake maturity (MP, UUUU) rather than treat all ex-China rare-earth names as a single basket trade.

items.headline: HKEX reopens today after Thursday's National Day closure; Hang Seng holds at 24,613 with Stock Connect suspended through Oct 7 for Golden Week
items.summary: Hong Kong's exchange was shut Thursday October 1 for National Day, holding the Hang Seng at Wednesday's close of 24,613.27 heading into today's (Friday) normal 09:30-12:00/13:00-16:00 reopening. Northbound and southbound Stock Connect trading remains suspended October 1-7 for mainland China's Golden Week and resumes only on October 8, meaning today's HK session trades without mainland flow even as the rest of the market (oil, Iran risk, Fed data) has kept moving over the past 24 hours.
items.actionable: The 0700/0981/1810 sleeve reopens today pricing in a day and a half of accumulated news (Iran escalation, ISM/claims, ahead of tonight's payrolls) in one session, and with Stock Connect dark until Oct 8 any move is purely HK-liquidity-driven rather than mainland-flow-driven -- expect wider intraday swings than a normal Friday.

items.headline: Houthi threat to Aramco's Yanbu hub and stalled US-Iran Hormuz talks remain the unresolved tail risk behind Thursday's oil spike
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis' September 25 claimed strikes on Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub (intercepted by Saudi air defenses) prompted France to commit troops and radar/defense systems to the site, and that threat remains unresolved even as this week's escalation has shifted toward direct US-Iran military signaling -- a third US carrier strike group en route, Trump weighing new strikes, and sanctions-relief talks stalled. Goldman continues to frame Brent within an unusually wide $80-120 range given how quickly the risk premium has swung in both directions since the Iran war began.
items.actionable: Thursday's carrier deployment and stalled talks are an escalation of the same Hormuz/Yanbu risk this item has tracked since late September, not a new, independent shock -- it reinforces keeping some inflation-hedge exposure in the silver/miner sleeve and some energy exposure rather than fading the oil rally as noise.

items.headline: MAS tightening odds build into the October 14 policy meeting as core inflation hits a 2-year high of 2.2% -- CIMB and OCBC flag a third straight hike
items.summary: Singapore's core inflation reached a two-year high of 2.2% in August, and CIMB Securities is now forecasting MAS will tighten the S$NEER policy slope for a third consecutive meeting on October 14, after surprise moves in April (+50bps-equivalent) and July. OCBC's Christopher Wong separately notes the Singapore dollar has held steady near 1.2780 against the US dollar despite softer Asian FX broadly, consistent with the market pricing in a steeper policy stance.
items.actionable: A third consecutive MAS tightening would extend the SGD-strength/bank-net-interest-margin tailwind that has driven DBS/OCBC/UOB's outperformance versus S-REITs this year, so the October 14 decision -- not Friday's payrolls -- is the next SGX-specific catalyst to watch for the bank-vs-REIT positioning split.

items.headline: China's Golden Week begins with PBOC gold buying at a 2023-high pace -- a structural counterweight to dollar-driven pullbacks
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added 20.2 tonnes of gold in August, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023 per World Gold Council data, extending a central-bank bid that has cushioned 2026 dips. China's week-long Golden Week holiday (October 1-7) traditionally marks peak seasonal local gold-buying, a potential source of fresh physical demand even as mainland trading itself is dark via Stock Connect until October 8.
items.actionable: The PBOC bid and Golden Week seasonal demand remain the slower-moving structural support under the silver/miner sleeve, distinct from this week's faster-moving Iran-driven safe-haven and dollar swings -- worth keeping in mind when deciding whether to add to the sleeve on any payrolls-driven volatility tonight.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds $83-84k band (last ~$84,677) as spot ETF inflows fade; Oct 27-28 FOMC remains the next real catalyst
items.summary: Bitcoin continues to trade in the $83,000-$85,000 range it has held since testing an eight-month high near $87,000 on September 21, last around $84,677. US spot BTC ETF inflows collapsed from a $2.4bn weekly haul (week to Sept 25) to roughly $134m in the final days of September, and that fading-momentum backdrop has persisted into October with no fresh ETF-flow catalyst reported since.
items.actionable: Bitcoin is still trading in lockstep with the same dollar/rate narrative driving gold and silver rather than offering portfolio diversification, and with ETF demand fading there's no case for adding to the crypto sleeve ahead of tonight's payrolls or the October 27-28 FOMC, which remains the next catalyst that could break the range.

items.headline: Tokyo core CPI due 07:30 SGT today -- forecast to jump to 2.4% y/y from 1.8%, a test of the BOJ's post-hike credibility
items.summary: Tokyo core CPI (ex-fresh-food) for September is forecast at 2.4% y/y, up sharply from August's 1.8% and well above the BOJ's 2% target, in data due for release this morning (07:30 SGT / 08:30 JST) just ahead of Asia's open; this print has not yet been confirmed in available reporting as of this file's cutoff. It follows the BOJ's September 18 hike to 1.25% on a split 7-2 vote, with the two dissenters arguing inflation was still running below target -- a hot Tokyo print would vindicate the majority and firm up odds of a follow-on hike, while a miss would hand ammunition to the dissenters.
items.actionable: A hot Tokyo CPI print this morning would likely firm the yen and lift JGB yields into Asia's open, a modest regional tightening headwind for HK tech and SGX risk sentiment on the same day as HKEX's reopen and hours ahead of US payrolls -- watch USD/JPY at the open for the market's read before the US print lands tonight.
